boot_instance_candidates.rva_or_api: libPS4 exposes sysctl/sysctlbyname; no privilege beyond the jailbreak
boot_instance_candidates.datatype: struct timeval (tv_sec 8 B, tv_usec 8 B, little endian)
boot_instance_candidates.why_boot_bound: the kernel writes the wall-clock boot instant once during boot init and never again until the next boot
boot_instance_candidates.changes_per_reboot: yes - a new boot writes a new instant; two boots in the same second only differ in tv_usec
boot_instance_candidates.evidence: libPS4 exposes sysctl/sysctlbyname (resolved from libkernel at init; the SDK itself calls sysctl with CTL_KERN for process enumeration) and the kernel-side OID is number 0x15 = 21 = KERN_BOOTTIME, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLTYPE_OPAQUE. Open point: whether libkernel on FW13.52 lets an unprivileged homebrew agent call it is not verifiable offline - that is why the confidence is MEDIUM and the kernel variable is the independent cross-check.

boot_instance_candidates.rva_or_api: RVA 0x224c6c8 (16 bytes: tv_sec, tv_usec at 0x224c6c8 / 0x224c6cd0), inside the kernel data segment; runtime address = kbase + RVA
boot_instance_candidates.datatype: struct timeval (two little-endian 64 bit words: seconds then microseconds)
boot_instance_candidates.why_boot_bound: same variable the sysctl node above exports; initialised once per boot
boot_instance_candidates.evidence: offline re-verification 2026-10-05: bytes at the RVA decode to sec 1789910256 / usec 860896 = 2026-09-20T13:17:36Z, i.e. the boot instant of the capture (the dossier was written about 47 minutes later). The sysctl handler for kern.boottime loads exactly this address (text-segment LEA to 0xffffffffd231c6c8 = static base + this RVA) and copies 16 bytes, so the sysctl path and a direct read return the same value. The only write to this address in the whole image sits in the internal clock-set routine (RVA 0x34ea16), whose callers are the RTC/inittodr boot path and the kern_time.c clock-set path.
boot_instance_candidates.correction: earlier W10 draft named 0x1a5ef80 as the boot instant: that address is in fact time_second (and 0x1a5ef88 time_uptime) - a pair that changes every second within a boot; corrected before review

boot_id_contract.algorithm: boot_digest = SHA256(JCS({'schema': 'ps4rf.boot-binding.v1', 'platform': 'orbis', 'profile_sha256': '<real profile hash>', 'boottime': {'sec': int, 'usec': int}}})); boot_id = 'BOOT-' + first 16 lowercase hex of boot_digest
boot_id_contract.accepted_primary_source: sysctl:kern.boottime (read-only userland sysctl, the same struct timeval the kernel variable at RVA 0x224c6c8 holds)
boot_id_contract.secondary_discriminator: kaslr_slide (never a source on its own)
refuse_when: boottime after the console wall clock
target identity does not match the profile
the two reads inside one session are not byte identical (BOOT_SOURCE_NOT_STABLE)
a simulated or test label is claimed as measured
boot_id_contract.note: W11 replaced the withdrawn W10 draft derivation (schema ps4rf.bootid.v1, which folded the target identity into the digest); the algorithm above is authoritative and the earlier draft string is not. A simulated second boot exists only as an offline vector and is always labelled SIMULATED_REBOOT_VECTOR.

open_questions: the live value of kern.boottime has not been measured on a running console in this project yet (W9 read no boot instant): either the agent calls the userland sysctl before any privileged step, or a minimal fixed callback copies 16 bytes at the RVA above

whether the sysctl call is reachable from the homebrew agent sandbox on FW13.52 is unverified offline (libkernel may gate it); the kernel-variable path is the fallback that only needs the existing one-shot privileged entry
two boots inside the same wall-clock second would need the microsecond field (and ideally the secondary slide discriminator) to stay distinguishable

no second boot of this firmware could be sampled for the boot instant offline: the live snapshot and the full RAM capture do not contain the kernel page holding the variable, so "changes per reboot" rests on the write-path analysis (RTC/inittodr boot path plus the clock-set path) and on the three observed different kernel bases, not on two measured samples
